Using the linearity property of double integrals, we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}(2-2x+9{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{R}2\,\text{d}A-{∬}_{R}2x\text{ }\text{d}A+{∬}_{R}9{y}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

The first integral is the double integral of a constant, so we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}2\,\text{d}A & =2{∬}_{R}\text{d}A \\  & =2\text{Area}(R) \\  & =2\cdot (2-0)\cdot (2-(-1)) \\  & =2\cdot 2\cdot 3 \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$

 

The function under the second integral is independent of $y.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}2x\text{ }\text{d}A & =(2-(-1)){\int }_{0}^{2}2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =3[{x}^{2}]_{0}^{2} \\  & =3({2}^{2}-{0}^{2}) \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

The function under the third integral is independent of $x.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}9{y}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A & =(2-0){\int }_{-1}^{2}9{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2[3{y}^{3}]_{-1}^{2} \\  & =6({2}^{3}-(-1)^{3}) \\  & =54.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, combining our results, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}(2-2x+9{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A=12-12+54=54.\end{aligned}
$$
